title: Santa Claus tradition traced back to the Sami
summary: Tero Isokauppila tells of Santa Claus tradition traced back to the Sami, about 8,000-10,000 years ago to present at New York, Netherlands, Germany, Italy, Turkey, Lapland, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.
place_text: New York, Netherlands, Germany, Italy, Turkey, Lapland

tellings.quote: If you follow the routes like how it came to the US to New York through the Dutch, the Dutch had Sinterklaas, their own version of Santa Claus.

plain: A Finnish mushroom entrepreneur named Tero Isokauppila, talking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, traces the Santa Claus story back through history to the Sami, the reindeer-herding people of Lapland in the far north of Europe. He says that if you follow the route backwards, Santa came to New York through the Dutch, whose own version was called Sinterklaas, and before that through Germany, Italy and Turkey, all the way back to the Sami thousands of years ago. If he is right, a modern Christmas figure would have very old northern roots.
